If you've been missing the ability to double-click the Digital Crown on Apple Watch to bring up the App Switcher—a feature that disappeared before watchOS 27—there's good news: it looks like it's making a comeback in watchOS 27.2 beta 2. Here are the full details.

Apple is working to bring back the watchOS App Switcher

Apple released watchOS 27.2 beta 2 to developers this morning, less than a week after pushing out beta 1.

There's one small detail included in this beta that should delight longtime Apple Watch users—including my colleague Zac Hall. Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 27 removed the ability to double-click the Digital Crown to quickly cycle through recently used apps.

He noted in his article that there's currently no way to quickly jump between recently used apps, and expressed hope that Apple would restore the gesture either before the official release of watchOS 27 or in a future update.

While Apple hasn't brought back the Digital Crown as a shortcut for the App Switcher in this watchOS 27.2 beta 2, it has reintroduced the App Switcher with a new gesture.

According to user Bones from the Apple Den Discord server, who shared the news on X, watchOS 27.2 beta 2 lets users bring up the App Switcher by long-pressing the bottom of the screen while using an app.

As Bones pointed out in their post, the App Switcher works largely the same as before: once users activate it by long-pressing the bottom of the screen, they can scroll through recently used apps by rotating the Digital Crown, or swipe left on an app and tap the "X" button to remove it from the switcher.

As with any beta, there's no 100% guarantee this particular gesture will make it to the final release (expected next month), but the fact that it's included in watchOS 27.2 beta 2 suggests Apple is indeed listening to user feedback and working on bringing the App Switcher back.

Do you miss the App Switcher on watchOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
